# Field Service Dispatch Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Field Service Dispatch Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 9 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded dispatch files, the proposed field-service connections and the intended channel; document blocked paths rather than bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for Field Service, telematics, certification and labor records, inventory and Teams, each with a dedicated least-privilege reference. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare operations, director, coordinator, duty-manager and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Dispatch authority | Have the operations owner name the dispatchers who apply safety, labor, SLA and emergency procedures before real requests replace the synthetic snapshot. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service operations owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Service-request queue, zone capacity and time to a dispatcher decision by priority Establish where cross-system review delays response before attributing a change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Request | Priority | Zone | Status | Required certifications | Eligible technicians | Time to dispatcher decision | Measurement period |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service operations owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Field service operations owner | Approve dispatch scope and escalation routes; confirm the authorized reviewers and production connections each response names. |
| Human dispatchers and field supervisors | Apply safety, labor, SLA and emergency procedures; keep every assignment, reroute, notification and field-action decision. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and record Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any dispatch connection is approved. |
| Field service connection owners | Approve Field Service, telematics, certification and labor, inventory and Teams access through dedicated, least-privilege connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-01 through FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-04 and the boundary tests on the current Draft; reject partial-ingestion answers and inventory mismatches. |
| Operations owner | Own production monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route dispatch decisions to the human dispatchers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for dispatch have named agreement.
- [ ] The operations owner records the current request queue, zone capacity and dispatcher decision points before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/field-service-dispatch/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and confirm blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and publisher prefix for the dispatch build are recorded before a build lane is chosen.
- [ ] The customer approves the sign-in requirement, audience and least-privilege scopes for workforce and customer-site data before any connection is bound.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/field-service-dispatch/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/field-service-dispatch/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/field-service-dispatch/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/field-service-dispatch/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Field Service Dispatch Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: field-service-dispatch-rules-and-controls.md
7. Add knowledge: field-service-dispatch-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_dispatch-dashboard
9. Add skill: aibast_emergency-response
10. Add skill: aibast_route-optimization
11. Add skill: aibast_technician-assignment
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-01: Field Operations Manager
15. Pass FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-02: Service Director
16. Pass FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-03: Dispatch Coordinator
17. Pass FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-04: Emergency Duty Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-01, FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-02, FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-03, FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the smoke test calls `FieldServiceDispatchAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes once in its own fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator decides each case; an annotated visual checkpoint does not replace it.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before technician location or customer-site details are shown. Request only the scopes that approved request, workforce and telematics sources need. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Field Service

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Field Service — read-write:** Bind read-only lookups first; gate any assignment write behind dispatcher approval.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Field Service:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Field Service:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Field Service:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Return the emergency response draft only; dispatch nothing and state that no field action occurred. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, assignment or notification succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved telematics and location feed

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service connection owners

1. **Bind Approved telematics and location feed — read:** Bind a read-only connector or MCP tool.

2. **Identity for Approved telematics and location feed:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved telematics and location feed:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved telematics and location feed:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not browse or claim live telemetry; use only the fixed synthetic locations. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report that no candidate qualifies; do not relax certification or capacity rules.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Technician certification and labor records

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service connection owners

1. **Bind Technician certification and labor records — read:** Bind approved read-only workforce data through a connector.

2. **Identity for Technician certification and labor records:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Technician certification and labor records:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Technician certification and labor records:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Return the emergency response draft only; dispatch nothing and state that no field action occurred. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report that no candidate qualifies; do not relax certification or capacity rules.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Parts and inventory availability

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service connection owners

1. **Bind Parts and inventory availability — read:** If adopted, add a reviewed read-only skill and tool.

2. **Identity for Parts and inventory availability:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Parts and inventory availability:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Parts and inventory availability:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not stage inventory or change the job; leave the decision with a human dispatcher. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, assignment or notification succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams and approved customer communication

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams and approved customer communication — write:** Gate any Teams or customer message flow behind dispatcher approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams and approved customer communication:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams and approved customer communication:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams and approved customer communication:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Return the emergency response draft only; dispatch nothing and state that no field action occurred. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, assignment or notification succeeded.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service connection owners

Bind least-privilege read connectors first; keep any assignment or notification tool separate, with authorized confirmation, current-state validation and an immutable audit event.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections start as least-privilege reads; any later write tool stays separate from analysis.
- [ ] No lookup, assignment or notification is reported unless an approved production tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test the approved deployment with dispatch and denied identities; a maker's working connection does not prove other users' access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic scores, capacity and hours are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations name the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact dispatch assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked dispatch corpus | All four cases, FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-01 through FIELD_SERVICE_DISPATCH-04, return every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Dispatch authority boundary | Any assignment, notification, reroute, dispatch, job change, inventory staging or customer contact is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reusable captures show a positive deterministic anchor and no blocker; reshoot-required captures stay withheld. |
| Release state | Both validated agents remain Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service operations owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service operations owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation from the approval owner.
- [ ] The approved dispatch audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Field service operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Field service operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Step 6-5. Operate

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review failed sessions, wrong-request answers, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Recovery is rehearsed with a restore path supported for the dispatch environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, knowledge use, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
